To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the X-FIR relation in normal galaxies can be explained in a satisfactory way by the star formation activity and that this relation is broken when this activity is absent, as for early-type galaxies.

the FIR flux is the best tracer of the star formation in normal galaxies, that the X-ray fluxes are the best tracers of the star formation for early-type galaxies, that the FIR fluxes and X-ray fluxes in early-type galaxies are linked by the presence of a central black hole and that the X-ray emission in late type galaxies is linked to the presence of an active nucleus.

the star formation activity is the link between the different tracings of the ISM, and that the X-ray emission in normal galaxies, not in active ones, is linked to the star formation activity, through its effect on the hot gas in galaxies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: 1. The relation between the FIR flux at 60 μm and the CO(1- 0) line luminosity for normal galaxies of all Hubble types.
the relations between the different tractors of the Interstellar Matter, and in particular the link between the soft X-ray and the FIR luminosities in non-active galaxies.

the study of the relations existing between the fluxes emitted by the Interstellar Medium of galaxies at various wavelengths, in particular in the far infrared, in the 21 cm, in the X-ray and at the CO(1-1) line.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the X-FIR relation exists only when a current star formation is active.
the X-ray emission of non active early-type galaxies is not linked to their star formation activity, as it is in late-type galaxies.
, in the frame of our theoretical model, the X-FIR link is present when the current star formation is still active and the galaxy is in the process of formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the X-ray emission in normal galaxies is not a good tracer of the current star formation.
the FIR-X-ray link, which is the most interesting one, is a good tracer of the star formation rate in the ISM.
the star formation activity is the key to understand the ISM tracers relations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the current star formation is present in a galaxy, it may link its fluxes at almost any wavelength, from X to millimeter waves.

in early type galaxies the star formation activity is not anymore the main source for the FIR emission, which is now dominated by a dust emission linked to the old stellar population, while in late-type galaxies the star formation is still the main source for both the FIR and X emissions.
the FIR-X-ray relation is a good indicator of the current star formation activity, while the FIR-CO one is not, as it is affected by the history of the star formation.
